answer: Willow-edge registration: each new agent must attach to k existing agents whose own neighbor sets already overlap, so the network only admits nodes that bridge tightly clustered regions. An opal score records how many distinct clusters a node's edges connect; low-diversity edges get throttled. Attacking requires building real overlapping neighborhoods per fake node, costing roughly k×(cluster size) genuine connections per identity, plus sustained bandwidth to keep vine-like edges live.
